- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 10–15 days after a sharp move, model should be adjusted downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion completes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 2–5 days; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment is trending upward.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillations (e.g., +0.3, -0.4, +0.3), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.  
- When true outcome is below 60% of 30-day average, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
